chunks: From him (Al-Hassan ibn Mahbub) from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii' al-Shami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Do not buy anything from the Land of As-Sawad (Iraq) except for one who has a dhimmah (covenant/treaty), for it is indeed spoils of war (fa') for the Muslims."

key_terms.أَرْضِ السَّوَادِ: The Land of As-Sawad, referring to the fertile plains of Iraq
key_terms.ذِمَّةٌ: A covenant or treaty, often referring to the status of those under Islamic rule with specific rights
key_terms.فَيْءٌ: Spoils of war or public property acquired without battle, belonging to the community

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying land in As-Sawad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the status of 'As-Sawad' as public domain (*fa'*), restricting private ownership to those holding a specific covenant (*dhimmah*), a ruling central to Shia jurisprudence on land tax (*kharaj*) and public wealth. It reflects the historical context where the fertile lands of Iraq were considered spoils of war for the entire Muslim community, thereby limiting individual appropriation to preserve communal rights.
